title: Chapter 1 - What Is an API and Why Use It?
description: Quick concept check on what an API is.

options.label: A set of rules for apps to talk to each other

explanations.overview: An API is a set of rules that lets apps communicate.

byOptionId.a: Correct. APIs define how apps talk.
byOptionId.b: Not quite. An API is not a database.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. An API is not a language.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. An API is not a browser setting.

questions.prompt: In the restaurant example, the API is like the:

explanations.overview: The API is like the waiter who carries requests and responses.

byOptionId.a: Not quite. The chef is like the server logic.
byOptionId.b: Correct. The waiter is the API connection.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. The menu is like documentation.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. The table is not part of the request flow.

explanations.overview: APIs let apps share data and features safely.

byOptionId.b: Not quite. APIs do not replace the internet.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. APIs still use servers.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. APIs are not about images.

questions.prompt: When your app asks an API for data, the API sends back:

byOptionId.c: Not quite. That is not part of API calls.
